question: to the Commission Laurence Farreng (Renew), Sabine Verheyen (PPE) Subject:

The rise of AI-powered interfaces is radically transforming the digital advertising landscape. OpenAI entered the advertising market in February 2026 and announced this week, at the Cannes Lions festival, that it is now ‘clearly established in the advertising sector’. Google has stated its intention to integrate advertisements into Gemini in 2026. These developments come at a time when media publishers are facing substantial traffic losses. According to Chartbeat data cited by the Reuters Institute, traffic from Google to media publishers fell by 17 % in Europe between 2024 and 2025. The emergence of AI appears to be accelerating the shift in advertising revenue away from media publishers and towards online platforms. 1.

Does the Commission intend to adopt specific regulatory measures governing the entry of AI models into the advertising market, in particular to ensure transparency and prevent a further erosion of advertising revenue at the expense of media publishers?

The review of the Audiovisual Media Services Directive (AVMSD) is scheduled to take place by the end of 2026. Does the Commission plan to use this review to introduce specific provisions ensuring that media publishers can recoup advertising revenue lost to digital platforms and AI?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (6.8.2026) The Commission has launched a call for evidence1 to examine the challenges arising from the use of copyright-protected content, including press publications, by AI models for training and output generation. The call seeks to determine whether further measures are needed to strengthen transparency, licensing and enforcement, fully taking into account the existing EU acquis, including the copyright-related transparency obligations under the AI Act2, as well as the Copyright Directive3 which provides for text and data mining exceptions relevant to AI and harmonises the legal protection for press publications. The call will seek stakeholder views on whether possible transparency gaps in the AI context exist in order to ensure fair remuneration for creators and support access for AI developers to high-quality data and AI innovations. The Commission is evaluating the Audiovisual Media Services Directive (AVMSD)4 and is preparing a proposal for its review. As part of this process, the Commission aims to further support the economic viability of the EU media sector, notably by strengthening the prominence of media services of general interest and modernising advertising rules to support the sector’s sustainability.
